records.text: Press release. Collaborative project safely disposing of over 1,000 drums of radioactive waste completes. From: Nuclear Waste Services, Nuclear Restoration Services and Nuclear Decommissioning Authority. Published 13 March 2024.

A drum from the Treated Radwaste Store (TRS) at Winfrith ready to be disposed of at the LLW Repository site in Cumbria. The project saw eleven consignments transported by rail from Winfrith to the Low Level Waste Repository in Cumbria for final disposal. The drums were disposed of using void space in Vault 8. The initiative made significant carbon emissions savings by rail instead of road.
The shipment of the drums by rail provided significant savings to the taxpayer and also saved 7502kg carbon emissions for each rail shipment compared to transporting these drums by road.

Project stats. 1068 drums diverted from the GDF. 830 tonnes of CO2 avoided by disposing in Vault 8 versus Vault 9. 7,502kg of carbon emissions saved by transporting via rail over road, for each shipment.

The Low Level Waste Repository in Cumbria is the UK’s primary LLW disposal facility. This nuclear licensed site enables the safe, secure, and environmentally compliant effective management and disposal of the UK’s radioactive low level waste.
